orderRegret.title: Right of withdrawal
orderRegret.intro: If you hired a service remotely, you can cancel it within 10 calendar days of the purchase. No account or explanation needed.
orderRegret.legalNote: Res. 424/2020 (Argentina) and art. 34 of Law 24.240. We email you a confirmation code within 24 hours.

orderRegret.notFound: We couldn't find an order with those details. Check the number and the email used.

workLaw.title: How we hire
workLaw.intro: We hire under the models of Argentina's Employment Contract Law 20,744 (LCT) and its reforms, and with independent contractors when the relationship truly is one. We pick the model by the nature of the work, not by convenience.

indefinite.title: Indefinite term
indefinite.summary: The general rule (LCT art. 90): no agreed end date.
indefinite.p1: Registered from day one, with social security contributions, vacation, bonus and full LCT coverage.
indefinite.p2: 6-month probation period (art. 92 bis): either party may end it without cause or severance, with 15 days' notice. Collective agreements may extend it depending on company size.
indefinite.p3: Probation periods can't be chained: if we rehire someone, we are deemed to have waived it.

fixed.title: Fixed term
fixed.summary: For work with a defined, foreseeable end, such as a closed-scope project.
fixed.p1: Its duration must be agreed in writing and justified by the nature of the activity; max. 5 years.
fixed.p2: If it lasts a year or more, we give 1 to 2 months' notice of non-renewal; otherwise it becomes indefinite.
fixed.p3: Early termination without just cause entitles the person to the compensation provided by law.

eventual.title: Casual work
eventual.summary: For temporary, objective needs outside normal business: a workload peak, a replacement or an extraordinary service.
eventual.p1: The cause is stated in the contract and must be real and verifiable; the employer bears the burden of proof.
eventual.p2: It ends with the circumstance that caused it; it is not used to fill permanent positions.
eventual.p3: The reason and estimated term are disclosed from the start.

parttime.title: Part-time
parttime.summary: Fewer hours than the usual workday, with proportional pay.
parttime.p1: The weekly schedule and time window are agreed in writing.
parttime.p2: Following the reform, only voluntary supplementary hours are allowed, never exceeding the legal workday.
parttime.p3: Rights and benefits are proportional to the hours worked.
parttime.law: LCT art. 92 ter, as amended by Laws 27,742 and 27,802.

remote.title: Remote work
remote.summary: A way of performing the job (not a contract type): the work is done off-premises using technology.
remote.p1: It is voluntary and reversible: no one is forced to work remotely without consent.
remote.p2: It guarantees the right to disconnect, expense compensation and the necessary equipment.
remote.law: Law 27,555 (added to the LCT as art. 102 bis).

freelance.title: Freelance (service agreement)
freelance.summary: Not an LCT model: it is independent work, without an employment relationship.
freelance.p1: Formalized with a service or work contract, invoiced fees and tax registration of the provider (monotributo or self-employed).
freelance.p2: There is real autonomy: the person organizes their time, uses their own tools and may work for others.
freelance.p3: If, in practice, there is subordination, the law presumes an employment relationship unless proven otherwise; so we assess each case.
freelance.law: LCT arts. 21 to 23 (art. 23 presumption, as clarified by Law 27,802) and Civil and Commercial Code arts. 1251 ff.

workLaw.note: This summary is informational and is not a job offer or legal advice. Labor rules changed recently (Laws 27,742 and 27,802) and some articles are under judicial review: the specific model is defined in writing for each hire.
workLaw.processText: We review your application, run a technical interview and tell you which model applies before anything is signed.
